items.title: Non-revenue water by DMA
items.why: Inflow minus billed consumption per DMA is arithmetic (IWA water balance).
logic: Daily losses = inlet volume − billed volume per DMA.
Loss share of inflow; flag a rise above a set level for 3 days.
items.example: DMA-02: 412 m³/day lost (18.6% of inflow), up from 13% last month.

items.title: Leak detection from night flow
items.why: Minimum night flow against its own 30-day median; no training.
logic: Flag +20% over the 30-day median for 3 nights (example threshold).
items.output: Leak alerts per DMA with the night-flow trend.
items.example: DMA-01 night flow 38 m³/h vs 29 m³/h median for 4 nights: probable new leak.

items.title: Burst alerts
items.why: Flow above and pressure below their hour-of-week bands at the same time.
logic: Expected flow and pressure per hour-of-week from 4–8 weeks.
Flag when both leave their bands for 15 min.
items.output: Burst alert with estimated loss rate.
items.example: DMA-02 02:40: flow +65 m³/h above band, pressure −0.8 bar: probable burst.

items.title: Reservoir level warnings
items.why: Hours to low level at the current net outflow.
logic: Hours to low level = volume above low band ÷ net outflow; warn under 6 h (example).
items.output: Warning with hours to low level.
items.example: R1 at 41%: 4.5 h to low level at the current draw.

items.title: Pump scheduling against tariff
items.why: Hourly demand profile (statistics), then pump hours chosen by a solver to keep R1 within limits at the lowest tariff cost.
items.other_inputs: Tariff by hour; tank limits; pump capacities.
logic: Solve pump on/off per hour: tank within 30–95%, min run 2 h, min cost (example limits).
Operator approves the schedule; SCADA executes.
items.output: 24-hour pump schedule with expected cost and tank trajectory.
missing: Tariff table and pump curves (master data)

items.title: Night pressure reduction
items.why: Night pressure above the critical-point minimum adds leakage; a fixed lower night setpoint answers it.
logic: Compare critical-point pressure at night with the service minimum.
Recommend a lower night PRV setpoint within limits; operator approves.
items.example: DMA-01 PRV night setpoint 3.2 → 2.7 bar; critical point stays above 1.5 bar.

items.title: Day-ahead demand forecast
items.reason: Needs a trained forecasting model (ML); the policy stops at optimisation.
